title: MANAGING DIRECTOR UTTARAKHAND TRANSPORT CORPORATION AND OTHERS versus NAVEEN CHANDRA KOTHARI
judges: ["Hon'ble Shri Justice Manoj Kumar Gupta,Hon'ble Mr. Justice Subhash Upadhyay"]

UKHC010125502026
2026:UHC:6658-DB
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
THE HON'BLE CHIEF JUSTICE MR. MANOJ KUMAR GUPTA
AND
THE HON'BLE JUSTICE MR. SUBHASH UPADHYAY
WRIT PETITION (S/B) NO. 484 of 2026
31st July, 2026
Managing Director Uttarakhand Transport Corporation & Others
........Petitioners
Versus
Naveen Chandra Kothari and Another ----Respondents Presence:-
Mr. Shobhit Joshi, learned counsel holding brief of Mr. Ashish Joshi, learned
counsel for the petitioner.
Mr. Sachin Mohan Singh Mehta, learned Standing Counsel for the
State/respondent no.2
JUDGMENT : (per Mr. Manoj Kumar Gupta C. J.)
1. The present writ petition is directed against the
order of the Uttarakhand Public Services Tribunal, Bench
at Nainital, dated 23.04.2026, in Claim Petition
No.75/NB/DB/2025, whereby the Claim Petition filed by
respondent no.1 has been allowed.
2. The brief facts of the case are that respondent
No.1 worked as a daily wager on the post of Conductor in
the petitioner-Corporation from 10.07.1986 to
18.06.1989. Subsequently, he was appointed on
substantive basis as a Conductor on 19.06.1989 under
Dying in Harness Rules in view of the fact that his father,
who had been an employee of the petitioner-Corporation,
died in harness. Respondent No.1 was subsequently
promoted to the post of Junior Clerk on 11.06.2016 and
on the post of Senior Clerk on 07.07.2020. After the
appointment in regular service respondent No.1 was
given benefit of higher pay scales after completion of 10
1

UKHC010125502026
2026:UHC:6658-DB
years and 20 years of service vide order dated 19.06.1999
and 19.06.2009 respectively counting his service from
19.06.1989 i.e. the date on which he was substantially
appointed on the post of conductor under the Dying in
Harness Rules. Thereafter, the ACP scheme came into
force and respondent No. 1 was given benefit of the said
scheme. Accordingly, he was given Grade Pay of
Rs.2800/- by way of second ACP since 01.09.2008. He
was also granted third ACP in the Grade Pay of
Rs.4200/-since 19.06.2015. After respondent No. 1 had
put in more than 30 years of service, the appellant-Corporation taking cognizance of the punishment order
dated 30.09.1989 in respect of alleged misconduct on
22.11.1987, when respondent no.1 was working as a
daily wager, by an order dated 15.09.2020, cancelled the
grant of third ACP (grade pay 4200) and sanctioned the
2nd ACP in grade pay of Rs.2800/- from 19.06.2009.
Thus, the date of grant of 2nd ACP in grade pay 2800 was
changed from 01.09.2008 to 19.06.2009.
3. The respondent no. 1 filed a representation
against the aforesaid order dated 15.09.2020 before the
Managing Director of the Corporation. However, in the
intervening period, the Assistant General Manager
(Operation), Pithoragarh on the basis of letter dated
11.11.2020 of the Finance Controller of the Corporation
2

UKHC010125502026
2026:UHC:6658-DB
passed another order on 26.12.2020. By the said order,
the benefit of grant of 2nd and 3rd ACP w.e.f. 01.09.2008
and 19.06.2015 was cancelled and respondent no.1 was
granted the benefit of 2nd ACP w.e.f. 19.06.2013. Thus,
the date of grant of 2nd ACP from 19.06.2009 was further
changed to 19.06.2013. By the order dated 31.12.2020,
the petitioner-Corporation cancelled the Voluntary
Family Welfare Allowance provided to respondent no.1 on
26.12.2008. By the order dated 26.12.2008,
respondent no. 1 was provided 10% of the Grade Pay as
Voluntary Family Welfare Allowance. In pursuance to the
aforesaid orders, the pay fixation of respondent no.1 was
done vide order dated 20.07.2021, whereby the
Corporation fixed the pay of respondent no.1 and
modified the date of grant of pay scale after completing
10 years of service from 19.06.1999 to 19.06.2003;
modified the date of 2nd ACP grade Pay Rs. 2800/-
granted on 01.09.2008 to 1st ACP Grade Pay Rs. 2400/-;
modified the date of grant of 2nd ACP (Grade Pay 2800)
from 01.09.2008 to 19.06.2013. The grant of 3rd ACP
Grade Pay of Rs. 4200/- w.e.f from 19.06.2015 was
withdrawn. This was done according to the petitioner-Corporation, on basis of various Government Orders,
which stipulated that if a punishment is awarded to an
employee for certain duration then the ACP would get
3

UKHC010125502026
2026:UHC:6658-DB
delayed by double the period of the duration of the
punishment.
4. The respondent no. 1 preferred representation
against the Pay Fixation Order dated 20.07.2021 before
the Assistant General Manager, Uttarakhand Transport
Corporation, Pithoragarh and the General Manger
(Administration), Dehradun. The representation preferred
by the respondent no.1 was rejected by the General
Manager (Administration) on 09.03.2022. The respondent
no.1 assailed the order dated 15.09.2020, 26.12.2020
and the order dated 09.03.2022 in Claim Petition
No.49/NB/DB/2024, which was decided on 19.05.2025
directing the Divisional Manager (Operation) of the
Corporation to decide the representation of the
respondent no. 1 by reasoned and speaking order. The
said representation was rejected on 25.08.2025. Assailing
the order dated 25.08.2025 and the other orders dated
20.07.2021, 26.12.2020, 31.12.2020 and 09.03.2022,
the respondent no. 1 filed a Claim Petition
No.75/NB/DB/2025, which was allowed on 23.04.2026
and the impugned orders were quashed and the
Corporation was directed to restore all benefits to the
respondent no.1. The said order dated 23.04.2026 has
been assailed in the present writ petition.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that
4

UKHC010125502026
2026:UHC:6658-DB
the action of the Corporation was justified and was in
conformity with the various Government orders, which
provide that the benefit of ACP can be granted on the
basis of satisfactory service and that, if a punishment is
awarded to an employee for a specified period, the grant
of ACP is deferred to twice the duration of punishment.
Learned counsel for the petitioner does not dispute the
fact that the alleged incident which resulted in the
punishment of stoppage of increments, had occurred
prior to the substantive appointment of the respondent
no. 1. However, he submits that as the order of
punishment was passed after the appointment of
respondent no.1 on substantive basis, as such, the said
punishment resulted in the issuance of the impugned
orders.
6. We have heard learned counsel for the
petitioner and pursued the records.
7. The learned Tribunal considered the fact that
the incident, wherein the respondent no.1 was punished
for allowing 13 persons to travel without tickets,
pertained to the period when respondent no.1 was
working on daily wage basis. The learned Tribunal also
took into consideration the fact that the alleged
misconduct was not considered as a disqualification in
permanent appointment of respondent no.1.
5

UKHC010125502026
2026:UHC:6658-DB
Consequently, the punishment relating to the earlier
daily-wage engagement had no bearing on the
subsequent permanent engagement of respondent no.1.
It is not in dispute in the present case that the services of
respondent no.1 were not regularised on the basis of his
previous engagement as a daily wager and that the
appointment granted to respondent no. 1 on 19.06.1989
was a fresh substantive appointment under the Dying in
Harness Rules.
8. A perusal of the record reveals that there was
no adverse material against the respondent no.1 after his
regular appointment. He was granted benefit of higher
pay-scale after completion of 10 years and 20 years of
service. Further, respondent no.1 was promoted to the
post of Junior Clerk and Senior Clerk owing to the
satisfactory services rendered by him after his
substantive appointment. The order of fixation of pay-scale of respondent no.1 dated 20.07.2021 reveals that
four increments of the respondent no. l were stopped
from 19.06.1990 to 19.6.1993 and thereafter, considering
the satisfactory service record of the respondent no. 1, he
was granted the benefit of pay-scale and promotion to the
higher post. Thus, withdrawal of the benefits granted to
the respondent no.1 after more than 30 years, without
there being any element of fraud and misrepresentation
6

UKHC010125502026
2026:UHC:6658-DB
on the part of respondent no. 1 in availing the said
benefit, was not permissible. The Government Orders of
the State Government, which formed the basis for the
issuance of the impugned order by the Corporation, also
does not stipulate that any past service rendered on daily
wages or contractual basis prior to substantive
appointment can be taken into consideration for
withholding the increment or for denying the grant of a
higher pay-scale.
9. Thus, we are of the considered view that there
is no infirmity or illegality in the order passed by the
learned Public Service Tribunal.
10. The writ Petition fails and is hereby dismissed.
 (MANOJ KUMAR GUPTA, C. J.)
